newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Anglo American offers to cut Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: Anglo American offers to cut Lonrho stake.

text.p: Anglo American Corp has offered to cut its 28.4-percent stake in Lonrho Plc, following European Commission opposition to it having control of the platinum division of the British conglomerate, a senior EU official said on Friday.
The official declined to be specific about the exact reduction, but indicated that the final stake would be in the region of nine to 10 percent. "It's about that", the official said.

The Financial Times said on Friday that the South African mining giant had proposed bringing its shareholding back to 10 percent, which was the level before the acquisition last November of 18.4 percent from Lonrho's former chairman Dieter Bock.
Commission and industry sources had largely speculated this would happen, as the EU took the view that the current situation was incompatible with the bloc's competition rules.
The Commission believes that Anglo and Lonrho, which together control a large share of the world's platinum output, would not longer compete against each other in that market.

The Commission is expected to announce Anglo's last-minute concession on Wednesday. But to ensure Anglo can get a fair price, it is unlikely to say publicly by how much the stake will have to be reduced nor how much time the company has to make the sale.
In similar cases involving divestments, the Commission often used neutral wording -- for example, saying the companies had agreed to take the necessary steps to restore competition.
"We don't want Anglo to be in a situation that it will be forced to sell part of the stake for peanuts," another Commission oficial said.

Anglo had been warned against taking control of Lonrho exactly a year ago, when the Commission blocked the proposed merger of the platinum interests of South Africa's Gencor Ltd, the world's only other large platinum producer, and Lonrho.

Anglo, however, always contested that its 28.4-percent stake gave it control of Lonrho Platinum. Lonrho controls 73 percent of its own platinum division, the remaining 23 percent being held by Gencor.

The Commission last year did not rule on Gencor's stake, only on the merger plans. That mystified industry obsevers, especially given the EU's tough stance on Anglo, but Commission sources said that Gencor acquired its holding before the bloc's merger rules came into force.

The Commission has the power to vet all mergers and acquisitions which affect trade in the 15-nation bloc. It has taken the view that the market for platinum, which is used in car catalytic converters, is global and has expressed concern about the three companies' ability to influence prices.

Anglo's platinum group Amplats produces 35 percent of the world's platinum output. Gencor and Lonrho together control 28 percent, according to a Commission statement in April 1996, when it blocked the merger between Gencor and Lonrho.
Gencor challenged the decision in the European Court of Justice.
